name: Best Buy Marketplace vendor program
why: Best Buy's Partner Portal has a public 'Marketplace vendor' application for merchandise sold online; the founder wants Best Buy as a launch retailer. Marketplace is the lowest-barrier public door; a ChannelEngine guide (secondary source) lists seller requirements.
why_now: Partner Portal onboarding guides page updated 2026-09-28.
ask: Submit the Marketplace vendor application once launch-ready; before that, read the Marketplace Standard Terms for claim-substantiation and product-listing rules.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK and no required subscription, launching consumer-side in May 2027. Before we plan retail, could I learn what Best Buy Marketplace expects from a new wearables vendor and which route fits a pre-launch brand? Happy to share a one-page overview.
entry_route: Public application via partners.bestbuy.com/become-a-partner ('Review materials and apply to be a Best Buy Marketplace vendor'). Registering does not guarantee business (Best Buy's own wording).
opportunity: Early online presence at Best Buy via Marketplace (third-party seller model) as a proof step toward a core-vendor or brick-and-mortar conversation.
unknowns: Per ChannelEngine (third-party, not Best Buy): US-based business entity, tech/tech-adjacent/seasonal categories, US TIN, US warehouse, ability to process returns, customer service by email, approval by Best Buy compliance and leadership. Marketplace fees/commission for the US not found (the $29.99 CAD figure was Canada only). Best Buy terms require documentation supporting any product claims within 5 calendar days, which constrains wellness marketing copy. Whether a pre-launch brand without sales history is accepted is unknown.

name: Best Buy new core vendor onboarding (Traditional Domestic / SDF)
why: Best Buy publishes onboarding activity guides for new Core (Best Buy owns inventory, store + dot-com) and Supplier Direct Fulfillment vendors, the route to the store shelves the founder wants; guide notes SDF setup takes ~2 weeks longer due to FedEx account.
warm_path: Ohio/Midwest retail trade contacts; none identified
ask: Read both onboarding guides to cost out the work, then ask a Best Buy merchant for the intake route for a new connected-health category.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK and no required subscription, launching consumer-side in May 2027. Before we plan retail, could I learn what Best Buy expects from a new wearables vendor and which route fits a pre-launch brand? Happy to share a one-page overview.
entry_route: Guides are for vendors already registered/selected; page says 'prior to registering' but the page I read does not show how a merchant first selects a new brand. Merchant-level intake route not found.
opportunity: Brick-and-mortar plus dot-com placement after May 2027 launch.
unknowns: How a new brand gets a Best Buy buyer meeting is not published on the pages read. Guide contents (steps, timeline, requirements) are in linked documents I did not open. Best Buy's old startup unit (New Blue / Best Buy Capital) appears defunct per a 2013 article; no current startup program found.

name: Amazon Seller Central + Brand Registry
why: Amazon publishes open registration for sellers and a free Brand Registry (needs pending/registered trademark and brand on product/packaging). Lowest-friction marketplace for a pre-launch wearable and the reference channel retailers check for demand.
ask: File a USPTO trademark application now (pending counts) so Brand Registry is ready by launch.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK and no required subscription, launching consumer-side in May 2027. Before we plan retail, could I learn what Amazon expects from a new wearables vendor and which route fits a pre-launch brand? Happy to share a one-page overview.
entry_route: Self-serve: create Seller Central account via sell.amazon.com; enroll in Brand Registry (free) with pending or registered word/design trademark, logo permanently affixed to product or packaging, product categories, manufacturing/distribution info.
opportunity: Direct-to-consumer marketplace listing at launch, with brand-protection tools.
unknowns: Seller fees, category gating/approval for wearables or health devices, and any electronics compliance (FCC etc.) were not read. Trademark status of 'Vybe' for Vybe Health is unknown (note other unrelated 'Vybe' companies exist).

name: Target Accelerators supplier intake
why: Target runs no program applications; founders fill one Supplier Intake Form and Target assesses fit across Target Takeoff / learning center / other opportunities. Target Forward Founders (CPG accelerator) listed 2022 criteria.
why_now: FAQ page current; Forward Founders criteria page dated 2022 (stale).
ask: Submit the Supplier Intake Form to get on Target's radar and access the Learning Center.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK and no required subscription, launching consumer-side in May 2027. Before we plan retail, could I learn what Target expects from a new wearables vendor and which route fits a pre-launch brand? Happy to share a one-page overview.
entry_route: Supplier Intake Form via accelerators.target.com ('We don't have applications'); submission does not guarantee business.
opportunity: Get on Target's radar early; learn mass-retail requirements.
unknowns: Whether Target buys connected wearables from new brands, and any minimums, not published. Forward Founders criteria seen (<20 stores, $5k-$500k lifetime revenue, physical product) were for a 2022 CPG cohort; current cohort status unknown.

name: Walmart Marketplace seller onboarding
why: Walmart Marketplace has a free, public seller sign-up with published requirements (business tax ID, GTIN/UPC from GS1, US B2C warehouse or Walmart Fulfillment Services, history of marketplace/ecommerce success); new sellers get a payment hold.
ask: Pre-buy GS1 company prefix/UPCs and apply to Marketplace after launch inventory exists.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK and no required subscription, launching consumer-side in May 2027. Before we plan retail, could I learn what Walmart Marketplace expects from a new wearables vendor and which route fits a pre-launch brand? Happy to share a one-page overview.
entry_route: Self-serve at Walmart Seller Center: five-step onboarding (verify business, payout, market details, shipping/returns). Requirements listed publicly.
opportunity: Second large marketplace; Walmart.com listing after launch.
unknowns: 'History of marketplace or ecommerce success' is required, so a pre-launch brand may be declined; category restrictions for health wearables not read. Referral fees by category not read.

name: Walmart / Sam's Club Open Call (via RangeMe)
why: Annual sourcing event with 30-minute pitches to Walmart or Sam's Club merchants; applications run through an exclusive RangeMe link. Requires US made, grown or assembled products.
why_now: Date of next event/registration window not found on the FAQ page.
ask: If Vybe's band is assembled in the US, build a free RangeMe profile and watch for Open Call registration.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK and no required subscription, launching consumer-side in May 2027. Before we plan retail, could I learn what Walmart Open Call expects from a new wearables vendor and which route fits a pre-launch brand? Happy to share a one-page overview.
entry_route: RangeMe application link released when registration opens; free RangeMe account recommended in advance.
opportunity: 30-minute merchant pitch for Walmart/Sam's Club and Walmart Marketplace.
unknowns: Hard eligibility gate: made/grown/assembled in the USA. Vybe's manufacturing location is unknown to me, so this may be ineligible. 2026/27 event dates and deadlines not found. FOUNDER DECISION: where final assembly happens.

name: REI Co-op Greenlight
why: REI's Greenlight portal takes a video plus application from any brand; REI says it contacts applicants within eight weeks and seeks activity-driven, innovative products. REI also hosts a vendor portal for product info after acceptance.
ask: Submit a Greenlight video application near launch (check on/off application window).
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK and no required subscription, launching consumer-side in May 2027. Before we plan retail, could I learn what REI Greenlight expects from a new wearables vendor and which route fits a pre-launch brand? Happy to share a one-page overview.
entry_route: Apply at rei.com/greenlight: product/brand video + application; decision within 8 weeks. FAQ answers (application windows, apps, review criteria) are collapsed on the page I read.
opportunity: Specialty outdoor/fitness retail with a recovery and sleep angle.
unknowns: Application window status ('on/off'), electronics/connected-device policy, and whether an app-dependent product qualifies are in collapsed FAQs I could not read. Third-party blog (TradeBeyond) mentions sustainability guidelines and a code of conduct; not verified from REI.

name: Costco vendor inquiries / Supplier Inclusion
why: Costco lists a vendor-inquiry page for non-food items and a Supplier Inclusion intake form for small and diverse suppliers; non-food prospects write to the corporate office.
ask: Check Supplier Inclusion eligibility criteria; defer outreach until Vybe has retail or DTC sales history.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK and no required subscription, launching consumer-side in May 2027. Before we plan retail, could I learn what Costco expects from a new wearables vendor and which route fits a pre-launch brand? Happy to share a one-page overview.
geo: US (Issaquah, WA; Midwest region office in Addison, IL)
entry_route: Supplier Inclusion intake form (eligibility criteria unpublished on the snippet read); non-food vendor inquiries by mail to Costco corporate (PO Box 34331 Seattle WA 98124 per page).
opportunity: Warehouse-club and costco.com placement, probably a year 2+ channel.
unknowns: Eligibility criteria for the diversity intake not read. The 'about $500,000 in sales' figure I saw was quoted by a Costco regional manager for CPG food brands (2024 trade article), not an official rule for electronics. Whether Costco takes novel wearables from new brands is unknown.

name: RangeMe (retail product discovery platform)
why: Many retailers source new products on RangeMe: Walmart Open Call and Walgreens submissions use it, a Dick's post points to it, 7-Eleven open call runs on it, and its supplier page cites 70% of the top 100 retailers. One profile feeds several channel doors.
ask: Create a free supplier profile (3 products) now; decide on Starter ($99/yr) when a retailer submission opportunity matches.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK and no required subscription, launching consumer-side in May 2027. Before we plan retail, could I learn what RangeMe retail buyers expects from a new wearables vendor and which route fits a pre-launch brand? Happy to share a one-page overview.
entry_route: Self-serve: free profile (up to 3 products, searchable by buyers); Starter $99/yr (unlimited products, direct submission opportunities); Premium $1,399/yr; Pro $2,499/yr per RangeMe's pricing page.
opportunity: Single listing that exposes Vybe to Walmart, Walgreens, Dick's and other buyers and gives access to retailer-specific submissions.
unknowns: Whether any buyer actively searches 'wearables' on RangeMe not verified. RangeMe 'Verified' badge criteria not read. Open submission windows change; check 'Immediate Opportunities'.

name: Dick's Sporting Goods new vendor submission
why: A DICK'S LinkedIn post (Feb 2023) says suppliers can submit via RangeMe to 'Become A Vendor'; an SPS Commerce article (May 2025) describes a separate product submission form and recommends LinkedIn buyer outreach. Fitness-first retailer in the same wearables-adjacent aisle.
warm_path: Pittsburgh-area/Ohio retail buyer network; none identified
ask: Submit via RangeMe once a profile exists; track buyer names on LinkedIn.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK and no required subscription, launching consumer-side in May 2027. Before we plan retail, could I learn what Dick's Sporting Goods expects from a new wearables vendor and which route fits a pre-launch brand? Happy to share a one-page overview.
entry_route: RangeMe 'Become a Vendor' submission (per DICK'S LinkedIn post, 2023); the official supplier-resources page rendered blank for me, and the SPS article names a different (third-party) form, so the current route needs confirming.
opportunity: National sporting-goods shelf and dickssportinggoods.com.
unknowns: Current official intake route unverified (two sources disagree). The DICK'S New Supplier Checklist I saw is for non-merchandise suppliers only. Electronics/wearable category openness unknown.

name: Walgreens new supplier submissions (RangeMe)
why: Walgreens' own prospective-vendor page says it uses RangeMe to manage new product submissions. Secondary guides describe first-party model and EDI/GS1 requirements; its diverse-supplier program status is described as possibly in flux.
ask: Register on RangeMe's Walgreens page and submit a retail-ready listing after launch.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK and no required subscription, launching consumer-side in May 2027. Before we plan retail, could I learn what Walgreens expects from a new wearables vendor and which route fits a pre-launch brand? Happy to share a one-page overview.
entry_route: New product submissions via RangeMe (Walgreens' own page). Established vendors then use SupplierOne/SupplierNet and EDI (secondary sources).
opportunity: Drugstore wellness aisle; strong FSA/HSA audience.
unknowns: Requirements list (EIN/W-9, GS1 GTINs, product liability insurance, EDI, proof of demand) comes from CrossBridge, a third party, not Walgreens. Whether Walgreens stocks a niche overnight wearable is unknown; one guide says routine essentials fit best.

name: CVS Launch (emerging brands, invite-only)
why: CVS Launch gives accepted emerging brands mentorship, leadership exposure and marketing support; applications are invite-only but an interest form is public and CVS contacts strategic fits.
ask: Submit the CVS Launch interest form once there is DTC traction.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK and no required subscription, launching consumer-side in May 2027. Before we plan retail, could I learn what CVS Launch expects from a new wearables vendor and which route fits a pre-launch brand? Happy to share a one-page overview.
entry_route: Public interest form only; applications 'currently available by invite only'.
opportunity: Mentorship plus potential shelf placement.
unknowns: Eligibility criteria, cohort dates and category focus not published on the page read.

name: Personify Health Developer Portal + Partner Marketplace
why: Personify (25M members) launched a self-service Developer Portal (APIs, free sandbox per Headspace quote) open to any digital health solution, and a Partner Marketplace whose 'Connected apps & devices' category lists Fitbit, Oura, Polar, Strava. Closest published route into employer wellness programs.
ask: Request Developer Portal sandbox access and a partner-intake conversation once DevKit v0.1 data can flow through an API.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health (Akron, OH). We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK and no required subscription. I saw Personify's Developer Portal and Partner Marketplace. Which tier fits a pre-launch device data source, and is there a path to the Connected Devices category? Happy to share a brief technical overview.
entry_route: Developer Portal (self-service) for integration; Partner Marketplace listing with tiers (Wellbeats page shows 'Certified partners' tier, subscription billing, eligibility thresholds). Portal URL itself not opened.
opportunity: Offer Vybe overnight HRV/recovery data as a connected device for employer wellness challenges and rewards.
unknowns: Developer Portal URL, sandbox terms and whether hardware/device vendors (vs digital solutions) are accepted weren't verified; the press release says 'digital health or virtual clinic solution provider'. Marketplace fees/revenue share unknown. Personify also sells its own Max GO wearable (possible conflict). Founder decision: whether to be an integrated 'data source' vs seek a bulk-device program.

name: Wellable (employee wellness platform + reseller program)
why: Wellable's employee-wellness challenges track activity through 'app & device integrations', mainly via aggregators (Apple Health, Google Health, Google Fit, Samsung Health) plus Garmin Connect, Strava and others; it also runs a reseller program. A device that syncs to Apple Health/Health Connect could appear without a bespoke integration.
ask: Ask whether devices that write to Apple Health/Health Connect count as eligible and whether a direct integration track exists.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health (Akron, OH). We're building a screenless overnight HRV/ECG band that will write to Apple Health and Health Connect. Does Wellable support devices through those aggregators for challenges, and is there a direct integration process for new device makers? Short question, happy to share details.
entry_route: No device-partner application page found. Path is (a) aggregator sync (Apple Health/Health Connect) or (b) outreach to Wellable.
opportunity: Employee-challenge data source with zero custom integration if aggregator-based.
unknowns: Integration list looks partly stale (Jawbone, Misfit, Microsoft Health), so currency is unclear. No public device-partner contact or terms found. Whether Vybe will write sleep/HRV to Apple Health and Health Connect is a product question.

name: Walkingspree channel partner program
why: Walkingspree (activity-tracking corporate wellness platform since 2006) runs a Channel Partner page for wellness firms, listing real-time data from Apple Health, Samsung Health, Google Fit, Fitbit, Garmin and more, and a partnerships email.
ask: Email the listed partnerships address to ask how a new device source gets enabled for clients.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight HRV/ECG band with a licensed SDK. Walkingspree lists several device data sources; how does a new device maker get supported, and are channel-partner terms open to a hardware brand? Happy to send a short overview.
entry_route: Public partnerships email on the channel-partner page (Partnerships@walkingspree.com).
opportunity: Reach employers via Walkingspree's client base and consultants; be a supported data source.
unknowns: Page is for wellness consultancies as channel partners (commissions, discounts), not device makers, so fit is indirect. Client count, pricing and integration terms unknown.

name: ONU Health (wearable aggregation API + ONU for Companies)
why: ONU sells an employer wellness benefit and a scoped API that aggregates Apple Health, Whoop and Garmin data for insurers, employers and health-tech companies; 'no self-serve signup, contact the team'.
ask: Contact ONU's team to ask about adding Vybe as a data source and a co-offering for employers.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health (Akron, OH). We're developing a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK. ONU aggregates Apple Health, Whoop and Garmin; could a new overnight-HRV source fit your roadmap or employer offering? Happy to share DevKit details when ready.
entry_route: Contact the ONU team directly (page states scoped integration, no self-serve).
opportunity: Add Vybe as an input to ONU's employer wellness benefit.
unknowns: Company size, customers, location and whether it adds new device sources aren't stated on the page. Partner contact name not found.

name: Medical Mutual of Ohio - MedMutual WELL (Vitality-powered)
why: Ohio's oldest large insurer (Cleveland; 1.6M members) launched MedMutual WELL in 2025, powered by Vitality with 'fitness device integration' for all group customers; Paramount Elite members were onboarded in 2026. Vitality also onboards devices through its own framework.
why_now: MedMutual WELL portal live for all members Feb 2026; groups migrated Dec 1, 2025.
ask: Find a Medical Mutual wellness/innovation contact via Ohio networks (JumpStart lists a Medical Mutual medical director as a Trailblazer mentor).
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK and no required subscription. With MedMutual WELL's device integration, who at Medical Mutual evaluates new wellness tech, and is a small employer-group pilot realistic? I'd welcome a brief call.
entry_route: No public startup/pilot submission page found. Realistic route: warm intro, or enter via Vitality's device ecosystem.
opportunity: Employer-group wellness pilot via MedMutual WELL's fitness-device integration.
unknowns: Device integration is Vitality's, so Medical Mutual may not choose devices. No named Medical Mutual wellness innovation contact or public pilot process found. Evidence for 'powered by Vitality' is a broker newsletter, not Medical Mutual itself.

name: Discovery Vitality (Vitality Group) device ecosystem
why: Vitality runs connected-device and wearables ecosystem (Apple HealthKit, Garmin, Fitbit, Oura, Samsung, COROS per a July 2026 job post) and a 'templatised device partner onboarding framework'; it powers Medical Mutual's wellness program in Ohio.
why_now: Job posting dated 2026-07-23 describes the device onboarding framework.
warm_path: Medical Mutual (Ohio) is a Vitality client
ask: Ask for Vitality's device-partner intake contact (US) and the criteria for new device onboarding.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health (Akron, OH). We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK. Vitality's device ecosystem runs a device-partner onboarding framework; who handles new device partners for the US business, and what does the technical bar look like? Glad to share DevKit specs.
entry_route: No public device-partner application found; the evidence is a South African job post and a partners page I could not read in full.
opportunity: Be a supported device in Vitality's reward programs used by insurers and employers (incl. Medical Mutual).
unknowns: Public application route, US contact, volume thresholds and commercial terms all unknown. Source for 'framework' is a job ad; the partners page returned only a title.

name: Cleveland Clinic Innovations - industry partnerships
why: Cleveland Clinic Innovations says it welcomes startups and corporate partners, offers an on-campus incubator, and shifted to an 'outside-in' model (Khosla Ventures collaboration, Oct 2025) to find external digital-health companies; contact numbers on site.
ask: Request an introductory call with an Innovations business development contact about an employee-wellness or research-collaboration pilot.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK, positioned as general wellness. Cleveland Clinic Innovations lists industry partnerships; could we have 15 minutes to see whether a research or employee-wellness collaboration fits your outside-in priorities?
entry_route: Cleveland Clinic Innovations partner page (industry partnerships; incubator inquiries by phone 216.444.5757 per page).
opportunity: Pilot or research partnership; employee wellness program; validation among cardiology-oriented teams.
unknowns: No public startup application form or pilot terms found. Wellness-only device may fall outside their clinical focus (their stated focus is medical devices, diagnostics, digital health). Incubator is lab/office rental oriented.

name: OhioHealth New Ventures & Business Incubation (NVBI)
why: OhioHealth NVBI helps third-party companies partner with OhioHealth and publishes a New Venture Submission form; criteria: aligns with strategic focus, primarily healthcare IT or services, solves a significant provider/patient issue. Responses generally take 15 business days.
ask: Submit the New Venture form framing the SDK/API as a data layer for wellness programs.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK and API for wellness and research apps. I'm submitting via your New Venture form; could we speak about whether an OhioHealth associate-wellness or digital pilot is a possible fit? Brief overview available.
entry_route: Web form at ohiohealth.com/nvbi/new-ventures-form; follow-up address printed on page: Innovation@OhioHealth.com if no reply in 15 business days.
opportunity: Employee-wellness or care-team pilot through NVBI.
unknowns: Their criteria say 'primarily healthcare IT or services'; a consumer wellness band may not fit, so the SDK/data framing matters. No funding or pilot terms published.

name: CDL-Cleveland Healthcare Delivery stream (University Hospitals + CWRU)
why: CDL-Cleveland launched May 27, 2026 as the first CDL site anchored to a health system; founders get UH as a 'living laboratory' and a nine-month program; no fees, no equity per CDL. Applications for the 2026/27 year closed July 24, 2026 per CDL.
ask: Ask CDL-Cleveland when the next intake opens and whether a wellness-wearable fits the Healthcare Delivery stream.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK. CDL-Cleveland's Healthcare Delivery stream pairs founders with University Hospitals. I missed the 2026/27 window; when does the next intake open, and would a wellness-data platform be in scope?
entry_route: Apply at creativedestructionlab.com/apply (2026/27 deadline passed; next cycle date unknown).
opportunity: Clinical-environment testing with UH caregivers; employee-wellness pilot.
unknowns: Overlaps accelerator category (JumpStart is in accel_events.json; CDL-Cleveland is not). Stream is aimed at care-delivery tech, so fit for an overnight wellness band is uncertain. Next intake date and selection criteria unknown.

name: Summa Health / HATCo (Akron) technology partnerships
why: Akron-based Summa (≈8,000 employees plus SummaCare insurer) was bought by General Catalyst's HATCo in Oct 2025 and on Aug 19, 2026 named its first eight General Catalyst-backed tech partners; HATCo's CEO calls Akron a 'test lab' for transformation. Hometown health system and insurer, but the stack is closed to date.
why_now: First eight partners named 2026-08-19; new CEO starts Sept 2026.
ask: Seek an intro to Summa's innovation/employee-wellness lead or a General Catalyst Ohio-network contact for a small employee-wellness or SummaCare pilot.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy, founder of Vybe Health in Akron. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK and no required subscription. As an Akron company, I'd value 15 minutes to learn how Summa evaluates local wellness technology for employees or SummaCare members, if there is a route.
entry_route: No public vendor/startup program found; the first eight partners are all General Catalyst portfolio companies.
opportunity: Akron-local employee wellness or SummaCare member-wellness pilot.
unknowns: Whether Summa/HATCo works with non-portfolio companies is unknown. No intake page, contact or pilot terms found. Leadership is in transition (new CEO Sept 2026).

name: CareSource (Dayton, OH) innovation pilots
why: Ohio Medicaid managed-care plan (2.3M members) ran a 2023 Ohio pilot with Cleveland digital-health startup Augment Therapy, showing it works with Ohio startups on wellness/exercise pilots.
ask: Ask Ohio startup network (e.g., JumpStart) for a CareSource innovation contact before cold outreach.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK, general wellness only. I saw CareSource's Ohio pilot with Augment Therapy. Is there a person who reviews wellness-technology pilots, and what does a small one look like? A short call would help.
entry_route: No public startup intake found; only a press release showing a past Ohio pilot.
opportunity: Member-wellness pilot in Ohio.
unknowns: Evidence is one 2023 release; current innovation program and any Medicaid wearable stance unknown. A consumer wellness wearable may not fit Medicaid benefits.

name: Life Time Innovation Hub
why: Life Time (190+ clubs) opened an Innovation Hub in spring 2026 for companies 'past the deck stage' in wearables, recovery and human-performance tech; accepted companies get opted-in members at select clubs, live pilots, leadership feedback and a possible long-term collaboration. It has a partner interest form; its Director of Performance and Recovery rolled out metabolic testing in April 2026.
ask: Complete the partner interest form (company info, product description, funding stage) once DevKit v0.1 units can be placed in a club pilot.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron. We're building a screenless overnight ECG/HRV band with a licensed SDK and no required subscription; DevKit v0.1 is going to a small group of design partners. Life Time's Innovation Hub looks like the right door for a recovery-focused pilot with opted-in members. Is the interest form still the best route?
entry_route: Partner interest form linked from Life Time's LinkedIn announcement (form URL not visible to me); a Life Time executive also posted a public email in the LinkedIn post. Applicant volume is high (mental-performance tools are ~1 in 4).
opportunity: Opted-in-member pilot at select Life Time clubs; potential long-term collaboration.
unknowns: Form URL not captured; selection criteria, fee/terms and timeline unpublished. 'Beyond the deck stage' may require working hardware. Whether the Hub is still accepting applicants in Oct 2026 is unconfirmed. Life Time also owns member-testing partnerships with other vendors (e.g., SpiroFit), exclusivity unknown. Ohio club locations not verified.

name: Anytime Fitness Preferred Vendor program
why: Anytime Fitness (5,200+ locations) accepts proposals from prospective preferred vendors through a published process; the US page lists a non-refundable $300 application fee and a panel that meets every 6 weeks (page dated 2016, fee may be stale); a 2026 India page shows a no-fee email process.
ask: Draft a franchisee-benefit proposal (US page asks for brand-specific proposal, $300 fee) only after confirming current US process.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight HRV/ECG band with a licensed SDK. I'd like to confirm the current US preferred-vendor process and whether a recovery or sleep-tracking offering could suit franchisees and members. Could you point me to the right contact?
entry_route: Proposal to the vendor-review address on the US page (anytime.vendors@sebrands.com per that page) with $300 non-refundable fee; US process dated 2016 so confirm first.
opportunity: Franchise-wide member perk or recovery-tech offering.
unknowns: US fee and email may be outdated (page published 2016-03-23). Must be able to serve all 50 states. Franchise-level decision-making means corporate approval does not guarantee adoption.

name: IAFC Technology Council (fire service vendor engagement)
why: IAFC's Technology Council is a forum for fire chiefs and vendors; its former wearables work includes a Wearables Subcommittee chaired by Ascent Integrated Tech's CTO (FirstNet blog, Jan 2025). Technology Summit International is Dec 7-9, 2026, Denver. Vendors are told to email the council.
ask: Email the listed vendor address to learn about the wearables subcommittee and TSI exhibitor/pitch options.
opener: Hi, I'm Jeremy at Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless overnight HRV/ECG band with a licensed SDK, general wellness only. I saw the Technology Council's vendor email on the IAFC site. Could you tell me how new wearable vendors take part in the council and in Technology Summit International?
entry_route: Vendor email printed on IAFC page (techcouncil@iafc.org); Tech Council form for practitioners.
opportunity: Learn department needs, find pilot departments, and get the data-privacy norms (IAFC Firefighter Bill of Rights) before pitching.
unknowns: Current wearables subcommittee status not shown on the new Tech Council site (its listed subcommittees don't include wearables). Exhibitor fees for TSI not found. 'deadline' above is the event start, not an application deadline.

name: Ohio Fire Chiefs' Association - ODC vendor expo / sponsorship
